job.title: National Commercial Manager
job.description:
National Account Manager - Own national sales growth, major accounts and commercial strategy

About the Company
Our client is a fast-growing, New Zealand-wide B2B services business operating in a demanding, operationally intensive environment. Continued growth has created the need for stronger commercial leadership, sharper pipeline discipline and deeper national customer relationships.

This is an energetic, hands-on business where commercial success is closely connected to operational delivery. What gets sold needs to be delivered well, and customer relationships have to be earned every day.

About the Role
Based in Auckland and reporting to the General Manager, you will take national ownership of revenue growth, gross profit, customer retention, pipeline, key accounts and sales performance. You will lead a small Auckland-based Client Services/Sales team while influencing regional and operational leaders across New Zealand.

This is not a sit-behind-a-dashboard sales role. You will set direction, coach the team, stay close to the numbers and still be prepared to pick up the phone, get in front of customers and chase the next opportunity. It is an ideal step for an experienced sales leader - or a high-performing BDM ready for a broader national leadership remit.

Responsibilities
• Own national revenue, gross profit and customer retention targets, with clear accountability for results.
• Build and manage a disciplined forward pipeline, looking several months ahead.
• Hunt new business, open doors and convert opportunities into sustainable revenue.
• Grow major accounts through regular contact, strong service and proactive relationship management.
• Lead commercial planning, forecasting and performance reporting, using the numbers to identify opportunities and address gaps.
• Lead, coach and hold the Client Services/Sales team accountable for performance.
• Influence regional and operational leaders to align sales activity with delivery capability.
• Manage pricing, rate cards, customer mix and margins to protect profitability.
• Represent the business in major client reviews, commercial negotiations, networking and industry events.
• Support tenders, major client onboarding, key projects and service-improvement initiatives.
• Travel regularly across New Zealand, with occasional client-hosting events outside standard hours.

Skills & Experience
• A strong B2B sales or business development track record, with clear evidence of winning new revenue and growing major accounts.
• Experience leading or coaching a sales/client-facing team - or clear readiness to step into broader national leadership responsibility.
• Strong commercial and financial capability across budgets, forecasting, financial modelling, pricing, margins and performance reporting.
• High EQ, strong negotiation skills and the ability to build genuine relationships with a wide range of personalities.
• A hands-on hunting mindset: you are comfortable networking, prospecting, cold-contacting and staying close to customers.
• Experience in utilities, water, power, infrastructure, labour hire, equipment hire, uniforms/workwear or another high-volume B2B service environment would translate well.
• You will ideally understand businesses where work must be continually won rather than simply secured through long-term contracts.
• Sector-specific experience is not essential. Transferable commercial capability, leadership potential and fit matter more.

Culture
The environment is high-energy, ambitious and practical. Leaders are expected to take ownership, keep momentum and work closely across functions rather than operate in silos.

The right person will be commercially driven without being overly “salesy”. You will know how to build trust, influence others and follow opportunities through to delivery. You will also enjoy the pace of a business where no two days look quite the same.

Benefits
• Take ownership of a genuinely national commercial remit.
• Work directly with an ambitious senior leadership team and influence growth strategy.
• Join a business in a strong growth phase where your impact will be highly visible.
• Combine strategic leadership with real customer contact and hands-on business development.
• Bring transferable experience from a broad range of B2B service industries.

How to Apply
If you are a commercially driven sales leader who still enjoys the chase - winning work, developing people and building long-term customer relationships - click the “APPLY” button to submit your application.

For a confidential discussion, contact Amanda Campbell at Farrow Jamieson on +64 9 915 9142

job.title: Care Home Manager - Auckland Central
job.description:
The Company

A well-established and highly regarded aged-care provider is seeking an experienced Care Home Manager to lead one of its Auckland care homes. Providing hospital-level and dementia care, the care home is focused on delivering high-quality clinical care and creating a safe, supportive environment for residents.

About the Role

As Care Home Manager, you will have overall responsibility for the care home's leadership and operations, ensuring high standards of clinical care, compliance, and service delivery, alongside strong operational performance and an engaged team culture.

This is a hands-on leadership role requiring a visible, supportive leader who can bring people together, maintain high clinical standards, and ensure the home operates effectively.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the day-to-day operation of the care home, ensuring a safe, welcoming and high-quality environment.
  • Maintain strong clinical standards across hospital-level and dementia care.
  • Lead quality, compliance and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Oversee budgets, occupancy, staffing and resource planning.
  • Build strong relationships with residents, families, staff and the wider community.
  • Recruit, coach and develop a high-performing multidisciplinary team.
  • Maintain your RN competency and provide clinical leadership and oversight as required.
What We’re Looking For
  • Current NZ Registered Nurse with a valid APC.
  • Proven leadership experience within aged residential care.
  • Experience within hospital-level and/or dementia care environments.
  • Strong understanding of aged-care standards, quality systems and compliance.
  • Sound operational and financial management capability.
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to lead teams, manage change and build a positive workplace culture.
  • Commitment to culturally safe care and working effectively with diverse communities.
The Offer

This is an opportunity to lead a substantial and well-supported aged-care facility in Auckland. You will join an experienced wider leadership team and have the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to the quality of care, team culture and day-to-day experience of residents and their families.

A competitive remuneration package and ongoing professional development are offered.

Apply Now

Please use the APPLY NOW button to submit your application or contact Kirsten Edwards on +64 9 915 9140 for a confidential discussion.

job.title: GM Operations
job.description:
Te Uru Amokura | Springboard Trust believe that outstanding leadership transforms schools, strengthens communities and improves outcomes for tamariki mokopuna. The Trust is a purpose-driven, values-based organisation that is committed to Te Tiriti o Waitangi as the basis for success in our organisation and education in Aotearoa New Zealand. Since 2007 they have partnered with school leaders across Aotearoa, bringing together expertise from the education, private, public and philanthropic sectors to build strategic leadership capability that creates lasting change. Today their programmes support hundreds of school leaders and have positively impacted more than 200,000 tamariki mokopuna nationwide.
Reporting directly to the Tumu Whakarae | Chief Executive, this role will provide the operational leadership that enables Springboard Trust to deliver its strategy, strengthen organisational capability and continue to scale its impact across New Zealand.

The Opportunity
This is a broad executive leadership role with responsibility for the day-to-day performance of the organisation.
Leading experienced managers across programme delivery, finance, people and capability, technology, marketing and communications, you will ensure the organisation operates efficiently, sustainably and in alignment with its purpose.
While strategy has been established, this role is fundamentally about execution.

You will build stronger systems, improve organisational effectiveness, strengthen financial discipline and ensure talented people have the tools, processes and leadership required to succeed.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead organisational operations across multiple business functions.
  • Champion a culture aligned with Springboard Trust's values and commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi.
  • Drive operational excellence and continuous improvement.
  • Strengthen organisational systems, processes and governance.
  • Lead financial planning, budgeting and organisational performance.
  • Support programme delivery that creates measurable impact for schools throughout New Zealand.
  • Build trusted relationships with partners, funders, government agencies and key stakeholders.
About You
You are an experienced executive who enjoys making organisations better and you understand that operational excellence and application of Te Tiriti go hand in hand.
You will likely bring:
  • Significant senior operational leadership experience.
  • Success leading multidisciplinary business functions.
  • Strong commercial and financial management capability.
  • Be culturally humble, curious and proactive in the way you build their Te Ao Māori, Tikanga and Te Reo Māori knowledge, skills and understanding.
  • A track record improving organisational systems and processes.
  • Experience leading organisational change.
  • Outstanding people leadership skills with the ability to coach and develop experienced leaders.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and influencing capability.
  • A collaborative, pragmatic and values-based leadership style.
Experience within education or the not-for-profit sector is welcomed but not essential. We are interested in exceptional operational leaders who can quickly understand a purpose-driven environment and make a meaningful contribution.

Why Te Uru Amokura | Springboard Trust?
This is an opportunity to join one of New Zealand's most respected education charities at an exciting stage of its evolution.
You will become part of an organisation committed to strengthening strategic leadership across Aotearoa | New Zealand through innovative cross-sector partnerships, collaborative learning and measurable educational impact. Springboard Trust works alongside principals and school leaders through strategic leadership programmes, coaching and strategic planning initiatives designed to improve outcomes for learners and communities.
In return you will enjoy:
  • A highly collaborative Executive Leadership Team.
  • Meaningful, purpose-driven work with national impact.
  • The opportunity to shape organisational capability and future growth.
  • Flexible working arrangements.
  • A supportive, values-led culture.
For a confidential discussion, please contact: Kirsten Edwards 099159140 or Iain MacGibbon 099159144
or apply using the “Apply now “button below.

job.title: Commercial Director
job.description:
About the Organisation
Our client is a multinational technology and business services organisation operating in a competitive B2B market.

With an established national presence and a strong customer focus, the business continues to evolve through investment in technology, service delivery and operational improvement. An opportunity now exists for an experienced Commercial Director to join the Executive Leadership Team and help shape the next phase of the organisation's growth.

The Role
Reporting to the Managing Director, the Commercial Director will play a central role in shaping business strategy and improving commercial performance across the organisation.

Working closely with the Executive Leadership Team, you will help guide strategic decision making, evaluate new opportunities and ensure the business continues to improve profitability, operational performance and long-term value.

You will partner across Sales, Operations, Service Delivery and Technology, providing commercial leadership that supports informed decision making and strong business outcomes.

The role also retains executive oversight of the finance function, ensuring sound financial governance, planning and reporting while using financial insight to support commercial decisions.

Key Responsibilities
  • Partner with the Managing Director and Executive Leadership Team to develop and execute business strategy.
  • Drive commercial performance through improved profitability, pricing, investment decisions and business analysis.
  • Support the evaluation of new business opportunities, strategic initiatives and growth investments.
  • Provide commercial leadership across key operational and customer-focused initiatives.
  • Identify opportunities to improve business performance and organisational effectiveness.
  • Lead the preparation and evaluation of business cases and capital investment proposals.
  • Oversee financial planning, reporting, governance and compliance across the organisation.
  • Lead and develop the finance function to provide commercially focused insight and decision support.
About You
You are an experienced executive with a track record of combining commercial leadership with strong financial capability.

You enjoy working across the business, partnering with operational leaders and contributing to strategic decisions that improve commercial performance.

Your background is likely to include:
  • Experience in a Commercial Director, Finance Director, CFO or comparable executive leadership role.
  • Demonstrated success improving business performance, profitability and commercial outcomes.
  • Strong commercial judgement supported by sound financial and analytical capability.
  • Experience influencing executive teams and working across multiple business functions.
  • Well-developed stakeholder management and communication skills.
  • Experience operating within complex, customer-focused organisations.
  • Relevant executive and financial leadership experience, with appropriate professional qualifications.
The Environment
This is a collaborative leadership team that values commercial thinking, sound judgement and practical decision making.

The role offers broad influence across the organisation, working alongside experienced executives to support growth, improve performance and contribute to the long-term success of the business.

How to Apply
To apply for this opportunity, click the APPLY button.

For a confidential discussion, contact Rhys Holding at Farrow Jamieson on +64 9 915 9147.

job.title: Executive Recruitment Consultant
job.description:
About the Company

Farrow Jamieson is an executive search and recruitment firm with more than 40 years in the New Zealand market. We are part of the Alpha Group of Companies, which include, Sheffield South Island, Emergent, The Johnson Group, Project Plus, Manamahi, Asset Recruitment, Alpha Recruitment, Triangle Recruitment, Healthwise Personnel and Staffwise.
We have built our longevity on a willingness to keep changing: adopting the best technology we can find globally, testing new approaches and continually improving how we identify and attract talent. Technology matters to us, but people matter more. We never lose sight of the fact that recruitment deals with people's careers, hopes and aspirations.

About  the Role
This is an opportunity for a Recruitment Consultant who wants to become more skilled, effective and commercially capable. You may currently work in a specialist discipline or as a generalist; what matters is your appetite to listen, change, grow and contribute to the team.

You will manage recruitment assignments, build trusted client and candidate relationships, and use contemporary technology and search methods to identify and engage the right people.
Duties
  • Manage recruitment assignments from briefing through to successful appointment.
    • Build enduring relationships with clients and understand what success looks like for them.
    • Identify, approach and engage high-quality candidates using modern search tools and technology.
    • Represent candidates thoughtfully, recognising the importance of career decisions.
    • Contribute ideas, knowledge and effort to the wider Farrow Jamieson team.
    • Keep developing your craft and look for better, faster and more effective ways to work.
Skills & Experience
We are interested in recruitment professionals who can demonstrate:

• Recruitment experience in a specialist discipline or generalist environment.
• Strong listening, communication and relationship-building skills.
• A genuine commitment to client satisfaction and high-quality work.
• Curiosity about technology and new ways of identifying and attracting talent.
• The capacity to accept feedback, change approach and keep developing.
Culture

Farrow Jamieson people do not talk about “hot desks”, “rock stars” or “ninjas”. We talk about client satisfaction, doing great work and enjoying the success that follows.

We are a supportive team that values professional judgement, continuous improvement and shared success. Our expectation is for people to commit to the team as well as their own performance.
Benefits
  • Grow your recruitment career in a supportive, professional, experienced team environment.
    • Use leading technology, sourced globally, to make search and engagement more effective.
    • Join a long-established national firm that continues to evolve.
    • Develop management and leadership skills within Farrow Jamieson or the wider Alpha Group of Companies.
    • Build deeper capability across client management, search, candidate engagement and recruitment delivery.
How to Apply
If you call, be ready to answer two questions: How do you know recruitment is what you want to do as a career? And can you convince us that you will listen, grow and contribute to a highly professional team.

Still want to talk? Click the “APPLY” button to submit your application. For a confidential discussion, contact Iain MacGibbon at Farrow Jamieson on +64 9 915 9144.

job.title: General Manager
job.description:
About the Organisation

Community Law South Auckland (CLSA) is a well-established community law centre providing free legal advice, assistance, representation, mediation and legal education to eligible people across South Auckland, Otahuhu and Franklin. With offices in Otara and Papakura, plus outreach services in Pukekohe and a Māori Land Advisory Clinic, the organisation plays a critical role in improving access to justice for communities that may otherwise struggle to obtain legal support.

CLSA is the largest community law centre by population served and is financially stable, with core Ministry of Justice funding secured through June 2028 and is financially robust. Its long-serving, highly experienced team reflects the communities it serves, with strong Pacific and Māori representation and a deeply embedded commitment to culturally responsive service.

About  the Role

Reporting to the Board of Trustees, the General Manager has overall responsibility for the operational leadership of CLSA and for ensuring the organisation continues to deliver high-quality, accessible and culturally responsive services.

This is a people-centered leadership role rather than a traditional corporate GM position. The successful person will work closely with a highly experienced team of lawyers and support staff, maintain strong community and sector relationships, oversee financial and contractual performance, and help the Board shape the organisation's next strategic chapter.

Early priorities will include building trust with staff and communities, supporting succession planning across a senior workforce, contributing to the next strategic review, and preparing the organisation for future changes in service delivery, technology and AI.

Duties
  • Lead day-to-day operations across CLSA’s Otara and Papakura offices, maintaining an inclusive, culturally safe workplace focused on staff wellbeing and retention.
  • Support the Board with strategic advice, reporting, risk management and implementation of the Strategic Plan.
  • Oversee budgets, financial performance, audit, resources and organisational risk, ensuring funding and contractual obligations are met.
  • Monitor service delivery, community impact and contractual performance while protecting service quality and equitable access to justice.
  • Build trusted relationships across Community Law Centres Aotearoa, government, justice, iwi, hapū, Māori and Pacific organisations, and community providers.
  • Lead succession planning and capability development across the team.
  • Guide practical adoption of technology, data and AI, while remaining visible, accessible and willing to step in operationally when needed.  
Skills & Experience
  • Proven senior leadership experience in a community, social service, public sector, legal, justice or not-for-profit environment.
  • Strong understanding of frontline service delivery to people experiencing disadvantage, complexity or significant life challenges.
  • High emotional intelligence, maturity and judgement, with demonstrated cultural competence and the ability to build trust across diverse groups, including Māori and Pacific communities.
  • Strong people leadership capability, including staff wellbeing, coaching, development, retention and navigating change.
  • Sound financial literacy, budget oversight, risk management and governance reporting experience, including working with Boards, funders, government agencies and external stakeholders.
  • Calm, practical and hands-on leadership style, with confidence managing conflict and challenging situations constructively.
  • Relevant tertiary qualification or equivalent professional experience. Legal qualifications are not required but exposure to government contracting, community law or the justice sector would be advantageous.  
Culture

CLSA has a close-knit, experienced and highly committed team. The culture is professional while informal, collegial and service-focused, with strong respect for cultural identity, relationships and mutual support. Given the often demanding nature of the work, empathy, humour and resilience are important.
The successful GM will be a grounded, emotionally mature leader who builds trust, listens well and values diverse cultures and life experiences. A highly corporate or hierarchical style will not suit; this role calls for someone accessible, practical and willing to roll up their sleeves when needed.

Benefits
  • Lead a financially stable organisation with a clear social purpose and tangible impact on access to justice, with core government funding secured through June 2028.
  • Work with a highly experienced, committed and culturally diverse team with a strong record of retention.
  • Help shape the next strategic phase, including succession, service development, technology and responsible use of AI, while building influence across the community law, justice, government and social service sectors.  
How to Apply

If you are motivated by meaningful community impact and believe your leadership style fits this distinctive environment, we would welcome your application. Please click the “APPLY” button to submit your CV and cover letter.

For a confidential discussion, contact Kirsten Edwards on +64 9 915 9140 or Iain MacGibbon on +64 9 915 9144.

job.title: Clinical Manager, Aged Care - Wellington Central
job.description:
Are you a proven Clinical Manager or a Registered Nurse with solid people management skills, based in Wellington or considering a move, with the type of personality that resonates and motivates people?  Want to work for a leader in the retirement village sector, one that invests in its people and puts the welfare of its residents first? We would urge you to consider this career option.

We are seeking a strong and natural leader to join our senior leadership team as we work together to foster a care delivery culture that supports the values and purpose of our aged community. 

If you are passionate about measurable and meaningful quality of care that meets contractual and legislative requirements and reflects current best practices, this is the opportunity for you.

You will lead a passionate team committed to supporting our aged care residents to live life their way.

This is a full-time role working Monday to Friday with some on-call requirements during evenings and weekends.

Qualifications
Our ideal candidate must have
  • At least 5 years of experience working as a registered nurse with a passion for aged care (and a current NZ annual practicing certificate).
  • Be committed to holistic person-centered care.
  • Have a calm and measured approach - able to problem solve and adapt to an ever-changing environment.
  • Be an effective and respectful communicator; highly skilled in written, oral, and interpersonal communication. 
  • Be able to build strong relationships with your team, residents, and whanau
  • Have experience with leading a team, including recruitment and development of staff and managing rosters.
  • Have strong organisational and time management skills.
  • Be InterRAI trained.
  • Engage with all our professional stakeholders to build strong local relationships.
  • Be resilient and committed to self-care.
Additional Information
What we can offer
  • A competitive market rate
  • An engaging and positive work environment
  • Ongoing professional development
  • Professional supervision
  • To become a part of the nationwide village community
  • Support to complete post-graduate study
  • A great local leadership team and ongoing mentorship
If you are looking for a role with a real sense of purpose and the opportunity to genuinely make a difference, this is the role for you! Please use the APPLY NOW button to progress your application or call Rhys Holding, Farrow Jamieson on +64 9 915 9147 for a confidential chat.
